newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Forum of the Poor members have laid siege to Government House after learning that their grievances have not been raised in cabinet. Ministers have difficulty in getting in and out as two main gates at Government House are blocked by thousands of farmers who have gathered there for two months to seek action on longstanding problems. (BANGKOK POST)

- The truck load issue is expected to be thrashed out today amid a warning by Sanoh Thienthong, the interior minister, of serious consequences if the limit is not lifted. A showdown is expected between Sanoh, who wants the limit raised from 21 tons to 28 tons, and Suwat Liptapallop, the transport and communications minister, who wants to see the present restriction maintained. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government has been urged to come out with a clear policy concerning the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) - focus on settling and recovering its debts or aggressively pursuing legal action against the alleged mismanagement of its executives and clients. The director of the BBC's legal affairs has complained about the lack of unity in government policy when tackling the BBC debacle, which has complicated the overall attempt to retrive the bank's bad debts. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand (BOT) will not intervene in the foreign exchange markets to support the value of the baht despite the fact that the currency was yesterday trading at a seven-year low against the dollar. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Asia Cement Co has received a licence allowing it to build a new cement plant and limestone quarry in the South. The plant, aimed at alleviating a cement shortage in the region, will be only the second to be built in the South. The first is owned by Siam Cement Plc. (BANGKOK POST)
